Lessons.Title: Equivalent Fractions on the Number Line
ExplanationParagraphs: Source IM2021 Grade4 Unit2 Lesson8 3-page original Student Task Statements PDF and teacher lesson read; the original title does not contain PLC Activity.

Warm-up Estimate shaded portion (10min): record an estimate too low, about right, too high, based on the teacher-presented original shaded tape diagram. Ask about 1/20 and 1/4 benchmark; do not invent the source image's exact shading.

Activity8.1 Handy Number Lines (20min): Andre partitions same-size fifths into tenths, fifteenths, twentieths: 1/5=2/10=3/15=4/20. Compare8/10=4/5 (yes),14/20=4/5 (no). Extend line beyond1 for6/5=12/10=18/15=24/20. Optional original physical human number line can use at least25feet of tape; teacher reviews the arrangement.

Activity8.2 Can It Be Done (15min): Priya2/3 can be6/9 and8/12 but not any whole-number numerator over10. On original number lines show1/10=2/20=3/30 and10/100. Reason mentally instead of constructing100 marks.
Lesson synthesis 10min: equal points on identically scaled lines and equivalent numerator-denominator multiples. Original human line, drawings and partner explanations remain teacher-reviewed.

Independent first-party Edulytics Cool-down 5min (NOT publisher educator-locked original): justify1/5=2/10, why2/3 cannot have an integer tenths numerator, and1/10=10/100. Teacher assesses reasoning; numeric exact Practice is supplemental.

KeyConcepts.Title: Refine a unit interval
KeyConcepts.Definition: Same location with more equal partitions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Beyond one whole
KeyConcepts.Definition: Numbers greater than1 stay beyond the unit endpoint on an equal-scale line.

WorkedExamples.Title: Andre's one-fifth
WorkedExamples.Question: Which fraction labels can represent one-fifth?
WorkedExamples.Method: Split each of five equal intervals into2,3 or4.
WorkedExamples.Check: Same point in all four diagrams.

WorkedExamples.Title: Priya thirds and tenths
WorkedExamples.Question: Can2/3 be written with denominators9,10 or12?
Steps: 10 is not divisible by3, no integer numerator.

CommonMistakes.Correction: Plot both on one number-line unit.
Extend the line to the right of1.
